The '''Swedish Mathematical Society''' (Swedish: {{lang|sv|Svenska Matematikersamfundet}}, '''SMS''') is a [[mathematical society]] founded in [[Sweden]] in 1950.
It is a member of the [[European Mathematical Society]] and is recognised by the [[International Mathematics Union]].{{r|ems|imu}}

The Swedish Mathematical Society organises two member meetings per year, awards the Wallenberg Prize annually, and organises conferences and scientific meetings with other mathematical societies.{{r|lms}}
It publishes a bulletin three times a year.{{r|lms}}
The logo of the SMS contains the third iteration of the [[Koch snowflake]],{{r|om_oss}} which was first described by Swedish mathematician [[Helge von Koch]] in 1904.{{r|koch}}

==Presidents==
The first president of the Swedish Mathematical Society was [[Arne Beurling]], and the second president was [[Åke Pleijel]].{{r|mactutor}}
The Swedish Mathematical Society elects a new president every two years, and traditionally each president works at a different mathematics department from their predecessor.{{r|lms}}
The current president of the SMS is [[Volodymyr Mazorchuk]].{{r|imu}}

==Wallenberg Prize==
Since 1983 the Swedish Mathematical Society has awarded its Wallenberg Prize to Swedish mathematicians under 40 that have a Ph.D.{{r|mactutor}} It is Sweden's most prestigious award for young mathematicians. The winner is the main speaker at the autumn meeting of the society.{{r|lms}}
